banner.label: GIFT CITY · IFSC
banner.heading: Set up, staff and settle your team in GIFT City.
banner.text: GIFT City in Gandhinagar is home to India's International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), which has its own regulator, the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA). ScaleAX is based here. We take you from choosing the right licence to hiring your team and getting them settled.

why.label: WHY GIFT CITY IFSC
why.heading: One regulator, foreign-currency operations and a tax regime built for international business.
items: IFSCA regulates banking, capital markets, insurance, funds and related services in the IFSC. Applications for IFSCA registration and the SEZ approval go through one online system, the Single Window IT System (SWIT).
IFSC units transact in specified foreign currencies. Rupee accounts are allowed for local administrative and statutory expenses.

Eligible IFSC units can claim a 100% deduction on qualifying business income for any 20 consecutive years out of 25, from tax year 2026-27. After that, IFSC business income is taxed at 15%. We confirm what applies to your structure.
A business district built for it
Grade-A offices, homes, schools, sport and leisure in one planned district, a short drive from Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar.

ifsc.label: IFSC SET-UP
ifsc.heading: Which IFSC licence fits what you want to run?
ifsc.text: Most global capability centres in GIFT City use one of the first three routes. Pick the one closest to your plan; we confirm the exact route in a scoping call.

routes.name: Global In-House Centre (GIC)
routes.summary: A unit that provides services related to financial products and services to its financial institution group.
points: Who qualifies

A financial institution group: banks, NBFCs, insurers, brokers, exchanges and similar institutions, and their group entities (parent, subsidiary, joint venture, associate, common brand, 20%+ equity or network member).
Who it serves
Group entities outside India, in jurisdictions not on FATF's high-risk list. Indian group entities can be served for up to 10% of the GIC's revenue in a financial year.
Operating models
Captive centre, build-operate-transfer, joint venture, hybrid, or another model IFSCA permits.
People
A Principal Officer and a Compliance Officer, both full-time and based in the IFSC.
What's not allowed
A GIC cannot be set up by moving existing contracts or work from the group's Indian entities.
Approval
Apply on SWIT. IFSCA grants in-principle approval, you meet the conditions within 180 days, then IFSCA grants registration.

routes.name: Global or Regional Corporate Treasury Centre (GRCTC)
routes.summary: A finance company or branch in the IFSC that runs treasury for its group: cash, funding, FX and risk.
routes.rule: IFSCA (Finance Company) Regulations, 2021 and the GRCTC Framework, circular of 4 April 2025 (amended 9 June 2025)
points: Legal form
A company, or a branch of a company incorporated in India or abroad.
Owned fund
At least USD 0.2 million at all times. A branch can maintain this at parent level.
People

At least five qualified staff based in the IFSC, including a Head of Treasury and a Compliance Officer, before operations start. IFSCA can relax this for up to one year after start, depending on activities and volumes.
What it can do

Cash pooling and liquidity management, intercompany loans and deposits, FX and derivatives (OTC and exchange-traded), re-invoicing, investing in financial instruments, managing bank and rating-agency relationships, treasury accounting, and acting as a group holding company. Factoring needs a separate factor registration.
Who it serves
Group entities of the applicant or its parent, and their branches, in India or abroad. Transactions with Indian residents follow FEMA.
Currency and accounts
Transacts in specified foreign currencies in the IFSC; may open a Special Non-Resident Rupee (SNRR) account for business outside the IFSC.
IFSCA fees
USD 1,000 application fee, USD 12,500 registration fee, and USD 25,000 a year.
Timeline rules

Provisional registration, then a Certificate of Registration. Operations must start within six months of registration (one extension of up to three months possible). A valid SEZ Letter of Approval is needed throughout.

faq: Most IFSC licences take about 11 to 20 weeks from first meeting to go-live, depending on the licence, document readiness and regulator responses. A GIC has 180 days after in-principle approval to meet the conditions. A treasury centre must start operations within six months of registration.
Can non-financial companies set up in GIFT City?

Yes. Professional and technology teams serving overseas clients can use the TechFin and Ancillary Services route. Corporate groups can run treasury as a GRCTC. Any company can take offices in GIFT City's domestic area, outside the IFSC.
What is the difference between a GIC and a treasury centre?
A GIC provides services to a financial institution group, for example operations, risk or technology for a bank. A GRCTC runs a corporate group's own treasury: cash, funding, FX and risk.
How many people do we need to start?

A GIC or TAS unit needs a full-time Principal Officer and Compliance Officer in the IFSC. A treasury centre needs at least five qualified staff, including a Head of Treasury and a Compliance Officer, though IFSCA can relax this for up to a year after start.
Can we move existing work from our Indian entity into a GIC?
No. The 2025 GIC regulations do not allow a GIC to be set up by transferring existing contracts or work from the group's Indian entities.
Do staff have to live in GIFT City?
They work from the GIFT City office. Many live in Ahmedabad or Gandhinagar; see Facilities for evening transport and homes nearby.
